title: Amazon: attackers used the Cairn AI tool to exploit a MONAI Label zero-day and take over a server, BleepingComputer reports
date_note: Date of BleepingComputer's report; it says the attacks ran 8 to 10 September 2026 and the maintainers released a security update on 18 November.
org: East Asian educational institutions (MONAI Label users)
geo_basis: region named by the source: mainly East Asian educational institutions outside China; no pin for a single organisation
summary: Amazon found AI agents running the Cairn tool exploiting a path traversal zero-day in MONAI Label, a medical imaging application, within 11 minutes of mapping its API, BleepingComputer reports. They gained root on a server. Amazon attributes it to a Chinese-nexus actor with moderate confidence. ThaiCERT (27 Nov) says MONAI Label 0.8.5 and earlier are affected and 0.8.6 or later fixes it.
plain: Amazon says attackers used an autonomous AI tool to find and exploit a flaw in medical imaging software and take over a server. Minuto da Segurança says a fixed version, 0.8.6, exists.
exec: AI agents were reported to go from mapping an API to exploiting a flaw in 11 minutes; organisations running MONAI Label should follow the maintainers' advisory.
action: ThaiCERT advises upgrading MONAI Label to 0.8.6 or later, enabling authentication, not exposing the server directly to the internet, and reviewing logs for requests to the /datastore/image and /datastore/label endpoints.

attribution.note: moderate confidence, from prompt language, activity timestamps and target choice, as relayed by BleepingComputer

validation.note: BleepingComputer and The Record (independent publishers) both relay Amazon's finding of a path traversal zero-day in a medical imaging application, used against a university and then a second one, since fixed by the maintainers. The Record does not name MONAI Label or give a confidence level; both rely on Amazon, whose own report was not read. Follow-up 23 Nov: Startup Fortune (22 Nov, relaying SecurityWeek and The Hacker News) says the fix is merged in source but not in a release, against BleepingComputer's 18 November security update; the GitHub advisory returned 403 and Amazon's post did not load, so both accounts are given. Follow-up 23 Nov: ENISA's EUVD record (read via its API) gives CVE-2026-133968, affected versions before 0.8.6, and says exploitation in the wild from September 2026. Follow-up 24 Nov: The Hacker News (24 Nov) says CISA added CVE-2026-133968 to KEV on 23 November; it states no fix or affected versions. Follow-up 25 Nov: Minuto da Segurança (25 Nov, relaying Amazon) says GHSA-qc22-rmgc-vg94 is fixed in 0.8.6 and notes no confirmed Brazilian victims; it gives no CVE. Follow-up 27 Nov: ThaiCERT (27 Nov, read) gives CVE-2026-133968, affected 0.8.5 and earlier, fixed 0.8.6 or later, and says CISA added it to KEV.

review.note: compared Amazon finding, 11 minutes, 8-10 Sep dates, moderate-confidence attribution, 18 Nov update vs BleepingComputer; 0.8.5/0.8.6, auth, logs advice and KEV vs ThaiCERT

evidence.quote: within 11 minutes, they went from mapping the application's API to exploiting the vulnerability
